profile.summary: EnCodon is a language model for protein-coding DNA that reads a coding sequence one codon at a time and returns a numerical embedding of it. The embeddings can be used as features or fine-tuned, and the package also scores codon variants by comparing model probabilities. It is part of the cdsFM suite, released with the generative model DeCodon, and was pretrained on coding sequences from the NCBI Genomes database.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each token is one of the 64 codons or one of 5 special tokens, and a start token and an end token are added around each sequence. EnCodon is loaded as a masked language model with rotary position embeddings. To embed a sequence, the wrapper runs the model, takes the hidden states of a chosen layer and averages them over the codon positions, leaving out the two special tokens. To score a variant, it compares the log probability of the alternative codon with that of the reference codon, either in the wild-type sequence or with the position masked.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Four EnCodon checkpoints are listed, in two sizes. encodon-80M and encodon-620M are the pretrained checkpoints; encodon-80M-euk and encodon-620M-euk are described only as eukaryotic experts. The encodon-80M checkpoint has 6 layers, 8 attention heads and hidden size 1024; the encodon-620M checkpoint has 12 layers, 16 heads and hidden size 2048. The configs of the euk checkpoints were not read. This page read encodon-80M at revision 81702e23, encodon-80M-euk at 746f9f3a, encodon-620M at 87958432 and encodon-620M-euk at 3597b284. A result should name the checkpoint and its revision.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Codon language model loaded as a masked language model, used for sequence embeddings and variant scoring. The record describes it as encoder-only; the sources read do not use that term.
facts.source_locator: config.json; README: Sequence Embedding Extraction with EnCodon; cdsfm/encodon/_auto.py

quotes.text: use the EnCodon model to extract sequence embeddings

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: encodon-620M: 12 hidden layers, 16 attention heads, hidden size 2048, intermediate size 8192. encodon-80M: 6 hidden layers, 8 attention heads, hidden size 1024, intermediate size 4096. Both use rotary position embeddings.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A list of coding sequences, read as codons from a vocabulary of 64 codons and 5 special tokens. Start and end tokens are added automatically. For variant scoring, a table with the reference sequence and the variant position and strand.

quotes.text: The tokenizer's vocabulary consists of 64 codons and 5 special tokens
token prepended automatically to the beginning of the sequence

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: An AnnData object holding one embedding per sequence (the mean of the chosen layer's hidden states over codon positions). The variant scoring method writes a log-likelihood ratio score per variant.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: encodon-80M and encodon-80M-euk: labelled 80M in the README; Hugging Face counts 79,982,853 each. encodon-620M and encodon-620M-euk: labelled 620M; Hugging Face counts 617,427,397 each.

gaps: Only the bioRxiv abstract (through the bioRxiv API) was read. The bioRxiv page and one retry of its full-text XML returned error 1015 (rate limit), so the full preprint, including evaluation results, training compute and hardware, was not read.
The abstract mentions models with up to 1B parameters, but no checkpoint of that size is listed in the README or on Hugging Face.
The sources do not explain how the eukaryotic-expert checkpoints were trained or how they differ from the base checkpoints.

The README embedding example leaves the input as a placeholder (seqs = ...). The script apps/get_embeddings.py reads a CSV or FASTA file and writes an .h5ad file, but the repository ships no example input for it.
At commit ce6f198d the saved repository tree (repo-tree.json, not truncated) lists no setup.py or pyproject.toml, so it is unclear whether the README's pip install works.

steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from cdsFM import AutoEnCodon

# Load a pre-trained EnCodon model
model = AutoEnCodon.from_pretrained("goodarzilab/encodon-620M")
PY
steps.explanation: The import and loading lines of the README example, wrapped in a shell heredoc. They download EnCodon-620M. To extract embeddings, the README then calls model.get_embeddings(seqs, batch_size=32) on a list of coding sequences, which the README does not supply. The repository script apps/get_embeddings.py does the same from a CSV or FASTA file you provide, and imports from cdsfm (lower case).

notes: EnCodon and DeCodon (folder 20-decodon) come from the same repository and preprint. The existing source gfm-guides-20261014-evo2-brixi2026-source-supplementary-information is the Evo 2 supplement, which evaluated EnCodon; it was not read. The bioRxiv abstract page was rate-limited (error 1015), so the bioRxiv details API record was used for the abstract. The code's default variant score key is codonbert_score and the training paths in config.json start with CodonBERT. These look like internal names; do not confuse them with the separate CodonBERT model (folder 19-codonbert).
